# Átropos: the restoration, the temple, and the world it opens
The domain you're reading about exists because someone refused to let **Átropos** stay *atropos*.

Hesiod names her with her sisters in the Theogony: Klōthṓ, Láchesis, and Átropos, "who give mortals good and evil." Of the three, she alone never appears as a character with dialogue — she is the act, not the actor. In the Theogony's first account the Moirai are fatherless daughters of Nyx, Night — older than Zeús himself, and in some traditions even the king of gods bows to their decree.  A second Hesiodic account makes them daughters of Zeús and Themis, law-givers by birth: the tension between fate above Zeús and fate as his instrument runs through all Greek thought.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Átropos
- **ASCII form:** atropos
- **Meaning:** "Inflexible, inevitable"
- **Domain of influence:** Cutter of Thread
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 2
- **Original script:** Ἄτροπος
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 46 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Ἄτροπος**. On the evidence, it means "Inflexible, inevitable".

Strip **Átropos** to *atropos* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **a → Á** — Acute on a: the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Átropos** lives at [/sites/atropos/](/sites/atropos/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/atropos/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/atropos/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/atropos/patterns/).

The restoration preserves one decisive feature the ASCII form drops — a single, honest mark — which places it in Tier-2: exact, and exactly labeled.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Átropos** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Insurance & Protection Services** — The measured span; actuarial science is her liturgy secularized.
- **Timekeeping & Calendar Systems** — The thread’s measure; the calendar of a life.
- **Legal, Justice & Compliance** — The verdict that cannot be appealed; finality personified.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/atropos/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.
